headline: Elon Musk, head of SpaceX, Tesla and xAI, rejects TSMC takeover reports for Terafab, and Intel stays involved.
score_reason: Pool 6 kept: statements by Intel's chief executive and Musk's X post are on the record.
importance_line: What changed: Musk now says Terafab will build and run its own plant and that TSMC could only sublease part of it, while the terms of Intel's 14A licence remain unclear; Tom's Hardware's view that a sublease would be unusual is its own analysis, not reported fact.
summary: Tom's Hardware reports, citing Bloomberg, that Intel's chief executive Lip-Bu Tan said Intel will stay part of Terafab, the chip venture of SpaceX, Tesla and xAI, and that Elon Musk, chief executive of SpaceX, Tesla and xAI, has rejected rumours that TSMC, the world's largest contract chipmaker, would build and run the factory. In our 4 Oct edition we carried a Tom's Hardware report that Musk had confirmed talks with TSMC; he has now replied on X that Terafab will build and run its own fab, and that TSMC may only sublease part of it.
notes: Follow-up of 1004:C08-01. Musk's X reply answers rumours that Terafab would partner with TSMC. Read in full.
